driver-layers.title: From pixels to pulses, on ESP-IDF
driver-layers.alt: Layer diagram: your application drives the WS2812Animator effects or a WS2812Strip directly; the strip turns pixels into RMT symbols and hands them to ws2812::RmtTx, which calls the ESP-IDF RMT driver; the RMT peripheral drives one GPIO connected to the first LED of the WS2812 chain.
driver-layers.description: From top to bottom. Your application, the only code you write, either runs an effect or sets pixels itself. The effects (WS2812Animator and WS2812MultiAnimator, the Effect values listed from inc/ws2812_effects.hpp) draw into a WS2812Strip. The strip (inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp, public methods listed) keeps the pixel buffer, applies the brightness and turns every bit into one RMT symbol with the configured high and low times. ws2812::RmtTx (inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp) owns one RMT transmit channel at 10 MHz and sends the symbols, blocking until they are out. Below it is ESP-IDF's RMT driver (the calls listed from rmt_wrapper.hpp) and the RMT peripheral, which times the pulses on the GPIO that feeds the first LED.
